sentence: I ______ breakfast at 8 o'clock every morning.
explanation: Se usa <have breakfast> para hablar de comer la comida de la mañana.
tip: Complete with the correct form of <have>

sentence: After work, I ______ home at 6 PM. My family is waiting.
explanation: Se usa <come home> para hablar de regresar a casa.
tip: Complete with the correct form of <come> — your family is already there

sentence: Excuse me, can you give me ______ to the train station?
explanation: <Directions> son las instrucciones que te dicen cómo llegar a un lugar.
tip: Complete with the word for route instructions

sentence: I always ______ up early on weekdays.
explanation: Se usa <wake up> para referirse a dejar de dormir.
tip: Complete the phrasal verb: ___ up (= stop sleeping)

sentence: She ______ on her coat because it's cold outside.
explanation: Se usa <put on> para referirse a ponerse ropa. Con 'she', se agrega <s>.
tip: Complete the phrasal verb: ___ on (= vestirse). Remember she + verb!

sentence: Please ______ down. The class is starting.
explanation: Se usa <sit down> para referirse a sentarse.
tip: Complete the phrasal verb: ___ down (= take a seat)

sentence: Can you ______ on the light? It's dark in here.
explanation: Se usa <turn on> para encender una luz o un aparato.
tip: Complete the phrasal verb: ___ on (= switch on a device)

sentence: I need to ______ out what time the bus leaves.
explanation: Se usa <find out> para referirse a descubrir información.
tip: Complete the phrasal verb: ___ out (= discover)

sentence: He ______ up his bag and left the room.
explanation: Se usa <pick up> para referirse a tomar algo con la mano. <Picked> es el pasado.
tip: Complete the phrasal verb in past tense: ___ up (= grab with your hand)

sentence: The exam was a ______ of cake!
explanation: El modismo <a piece of cake> significa algo muy fácil.
tip: Complete the idiom: a ___ of cake (= very easy)

sentence: I'm feeling a bit under the ______ today.
explanation: El modismo <under the weather> significa sentirse enfermo o mal.
tip: Complete the idiom: under the ___ (= feeling sick)

sentence: It's late. Let's ______ it a day.
explanation: El modismo <call it a day> significa dejar de trabajar por hoy.
tip: Complete the idiom: ___ it a day (= stop working)

sentence: ______ a leg at your performance tonight!
explanation: El modismo <break a leg> significa 'buena suerte'.
tip: Complete the idiom: ___ a leg! (= good luck)

sentence: I need to hit the ______ for my test tomorrow.
explanation: El modismo <hit the books> significa empezar a estudiar.
tip: Complete the idiom: hit the ___ (= start studying)

sentence: Keep an ______ on your little brother, please.
explanation: El modismo <keep an eye on> significa vigilar con atención.
tip: Complete the idiom: keep an ___ on (= watch carefully)

sentence: I ______ to bed at 10 PM every night.
explanation: Se usa <go to bed> para hablar de irse a dormir.
tip: Complete the expression: ___ to bed

sentence: She ______ a shower before breakfast.
explanation: Se usa <take a shower> para referirse a ducharse. Con 'she', se usa <takes>.
tip: The collocation is <take> a shower — conjugate for she

sentence: I ______ the bus to school every day.
explanation: Se usa <take the bus> para referirse a usar el autobús como transporte.
tip: The collocation is <take> the bus — conjugate for I

sentence: Can I ______ you a question?
explanation: Se usa <ask> para pedir información.
tip: Complete with the verb used before 'a question'

sentence: I don't ______ that word.
explanation: Se usa <understand> cuando algo no está claro.
tip: Complete with the verb that means 'to comprehend'
